title: The GlobalFoundries CEO and his Kotura-pedigree lead independent
body:
## The Semiconductor Process Man

Suresh Venkatesan arrived at POET Technologies in 2015 carrying credentials that would have seemed eccentric for a photonics company at the time. His B.Tech from the Indian Institute of Technology, a master's and doctorate in electrical engineering from Purdue, and a career trajectory through Motorola, Freescale Semiconductor, and GlobalFoundries had produced an executive whose entire professional formation was in semiconductor process development — not photonics. Motorola inducted him into its Scientific Advisory Board Associates programme in 2004. Freescale named him a Freescale Fellow in 2007, recognising his contributions to CMOS technology. Then, in 2009, he moved to GlobalFoundries as Senior Vice President of Technology Development.

That GlobalFoundries chapter is the single most concrete operating credential Venkatesan carried into POET. The 28-nanometre ramp he led at GlobalFoundries placed him at the intersection of one of the most contested competitive episodes in foundry history — the period when GlobalFoundries, Samsung, and TSMC were fighting for leadership-node share against a backdrop of enormous hyperscaler capital expenditure. He was also instrumental in the 14nm technology transfer and qualification programme that followed. Leading a process node ramp at a tier-one foundry is categorically different from managing a photonics startup's engineering team; it requires translating theoretical process physics into high-yield, high-volume manufacturing at a cadence that serves actual customers. Over a career spanning both Freescale and GlobalFoundries, Venkatesan accumulated more than 25 US patents and co-authored over 50 technical papers.

The logic of hiring him as Chairman and CEO of POET — then a development-stage compound-semiconductor company with a pre-commercial platform thesis — becomes legible only if one accepts the company's own architectural premise: that the Optical Interposer is fundamentally a wafer-level semiconductor manufacturing discipline, not an optics assembly problem. Venkatesan's job, as he articulated it, was to bring semiconductor process rigour to a platform that had previously been governed more as a research project. Whether that bet was correctly placed will be answered by hyperscaler qualification decisions in 2026 and 2027. What is not in dispute is that the operational credibility of the pitch — that POET's interposer can be manufactured with foundry-grade consistency — rests substantially on his personal biography.

## The Kotura Precedent

Jean-Louis Malinge joined POET's board as Lead Independent Director in September 2017. His framing within the POET governance structure is simple and important: he is the only person on the board who has already done the thing POET is trying to do. From 2004 to 2013, Malinge served as President and CEO of Kotura, a silicon photonics company whose products were deployed inside three of the top five telecommunications companies in the world. In 2013, Mellanox Technologies [acquired Kotura for $82 million](https://www.poet-technologies.com/team/jean-louis-malinge), providing a concrete exit at a credible valuation for a pre-revenue-at-scale silicon photonics platform. Malinge ran the company from early-stage through that sale.

Before Kotura, Malinge spent more than fifteen years at Corning Incorporated, ultimately as Vice President of Optical Networking Components — a tenure that gave him deep product and customer knowledge across the optical communications stack before he moved into a platform-company operating role. Since the Kotura sale, he has served as a Partner at ARCH Venture Partners, a Chicago-based early-stage venture firm managing approximately $2 billion in assets under management, and as Managing Director at YADAIS, his photonics and telecoms consulting practice.

The Kotura/Mellanox precedent is the most direct analogue available for the POET investment thesis. Kotura built a silicon-photonic integration platform, qualified it with tier-one telecom customers, and sold to a semiconductor company — Mellanox — that subsequently wanted the technology for data-centre networking applications. POET is attempting a structurally similar journey with a different integration architecture (the Optical Interposer rather than silicon-on-insulator), a different primary customer segment (hyperscaler AI infrastructure rather than telecom), and a larger addressable market. Malinge's presence on the board as Lead Independent Director carries an implicit signal: someone who successfully navigated a silicon-photonics platform from development through exit finds POET's architecture and market thesis credible enough to govern.

## The Working Hyperscaler Credential

Theresa Lan Ende joined POET's board as a formal director in October 2022, having served as an advisor since June of that year. Her primary job at the snapshot date remained Chief Procurement Officer at Arista Networks — a role she had grown into from a decade as Senior Director of Global Supply Chain Management at the same company.

The significance of Lan Ende's seat on the POET board is not biographical; it is structural. Arista Networks is one of the dominant vendors of high-speed Ethernet switching equipment into hyperscaler AI infrastructure builds. Its customers include the organisations that will ultimately decide whether co-packaged optics becomes a volume procurement category or remains a pilot programme at the periphery of data-centre design. Lan Ende's career — which ran through JDS Uniphase, Force10 Networks, Cisco Systems, and ROLM Telecommunications before her decade-plus at Arista — is supply-chain-heavy in exactly the optical and switching domains POET targets. The Silicon Valley Business Journal named her among its Top 100 Women of Influence in 2019.

A working CPO at a hyperscaler-adjacent switching company occupies a seat on POET's board while the company is seeking qualifications in hyperscaler co-packaged optics supply chains. The governance optics are straightforward. The practical question — whether Lan Ende's position at Arista translates into any direct pathway for POET's interposer into switching-platform designs — is unanswerable from public disclosures. What is answerable is that POET's board understood, in recruiting her, exactly what kind of credential gap it was filling.

## Thirty-Two Years of Optoelectronics

Glen Riley joined POET's board in December 2020 and chairs its Compensation Committee. His career defies tidy summary but rewards enumeration: Asia Sales President at Lucent Technologies Microelectronics Group, based in Tokyo; Vice President at Agere Systems responsible for its high-speed and long-haul optoelectronics business; Chief Executive of Opticalis, an optical component start-up; General Manager of TriQuint Optoelectronics; General Manager of TriQuint's GaAs Foundry Business; Managing Director of TriQuint International in Singapore; and, most recently, General Manager of the Filter Solutions Business Unit at Qorvo. He graduated valedictorian from the School of Engineering at the University of Maine and completed Harvard Business School's General Management Programme in 1998.

The TriQuint years are particularly relevant to POET's technology positioning. Running a GaAs foundry business requires the same compound-semiconductor process discipline that POET's Optical Interposer architecture depends on — III-V materials, epitaxial growth, wafer-level integration — applied to a volume manufacturing context with real customers and real yield targets. Riley had three distinct subsidiary general-manager roles inside TriQuint before the company merged with RF Micro Devices to form Qorvo in 2015. Thirty-two years of compound-semiconductor and optoelectronics operating experience, distributed across multiple business unit leadership positions, is the depth of domain knowledge that a pre-revenue photonics platform company can rarely attract to its board.

## The CFO Credential and the Audit Chair Reconfiguration

Robert Tirva joined POET's board in December 2024 and became an Audit Committee member. His most recent operating role was as President, Chief Operating Officer, and Chief Financial Officer of Sonim Technologies, a ruggedised mobile device company acquired by AJP Holding Company in 2022. Earlier positions spanned IBM, Broadcom Corporation, Dropbox, and Intermedia Cloud Communications. His current external board commitments include Skyworks Aeronautics.

The timing of Tirva's arrival is inseparable from what followed: at the June 2025 Annual General and Special Meeting, Chris Tsiofas retired from the POET board after thirteen years as Audit Committee Chair. Tsiofas's tenure spanned the full arc of POET's modern corporate history — the pivot from a development-stage compound-semiconductor research programme to the Optical Interposer platform thesis, the Singapore manufacturing buildout, and the $250 million institutional equity raise that produced the $313 million cash position. His departure cleared the Audit Committee Chair seat; Tirva, carrying a combined CFO-COO-President credential from a public-company operating role, is the natural successor. The audit chair reconfiguration is the most consequential governance event of the 2024-2025 period and marked an orderly transition rather than a rupture.

One structural observation belongs here: POET's public team page lists no separate Chief Financial Officer. For a company holding $313.4 million in cash and short-term investments and filing a 20-F with the SEC as a foreign private issuer, the absence of a named CFO is structurally noteworthy. The financial function is presumably managed through corporate-level finance and the Audit Committee, with Tirva's arrival providing the requisite oversight credential. Investors reviewing POET's governance should note this gap explicitly.

## The Newest Arrival and the M&A Pattern

Sohail Khan joined POET's board on July 7, 2025, assigned to the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee. His career carries the deepest chip-CEO M&A pattern recognition of any director on the board. At Coherent Corp. — the compound-semiconductor materials and components company formerly known as II-VI — Khan served as Executive Vice President of Wideband Gap Electronics and President of SiC, LLC, giving him operating responsibility inside one of the dominant III-V and silicon-carbide materials companies in the industry. Before Coherent, he served as CEO and Head of Strategy at Agere Systems, as President and CEO of fabless semiconductor company ViXS Systems, and as Managing Partner at K5 Innovations. His board tenures include sixteen years at LightPath Technologies, an optical-component company, and a director seat at Intersil Corporation.

The Coherent SiC credential is the most structurally adjacent operating role to POET's technology stack. Silicon carbide and the III-V compound semiconductors POET works with are both wide-bandgap or compound-semiconductor materials categories where wafer-level process discipline and materials-science depth are the moat. Running a SiC business unit inside Coherent is not the same as running a photonic interposer company, but the operational vocabulary is recognisably similar. Khan's Agere and ViXS CEO roles bring something different: pattern recognition across semiconductor company M&A cycles at multiple scale points — Agere was itself a spin-off from Lucent Technologies and was subsequently acquired by LSI Corporation in 2007.

## A Board Calibrated for One Decision

The six-director board POET carried into mid-2026 — Venkatesan, Malinge, Lan Ende, Riley, Tirva, Khan — is unusually well-credentialed for a company at its revenue stage. The composition reads as a deliberate answer to the single question the Optical Interposer thesis must answer over the next eighteen to twenty-four months: can POET get qualified in a hyperscaler CPO supply chain before competing architectures lock it out or pluggable optics continue to absorb the addressable market?

Against that question, every seat has a legible function. Venkatesan brings foundry-process discipline to the CEO chair. Malinge brings the only direct operating precedent — having done the silicon-photonics company-and-exit once already. Lan Ende brings the customer-side supply-chain credential at a hyperscaler-adjacent company. Riley brings 32 years of compound-semiconductor and optoelectronics operating depth. Tirva brings the public-company financial-execution credential the reconfigured audit function requires. Khan brings chip-CEO M&A pattern recognition and Coherent-grade compound-semiconductor operating experience.

Compare this with a board assembled for IPO execution or transformational M&A — typically heavy on investment-banking relationships, capital-markets advisors, and financial-engineering expertise. POET's board contains none of that. It is calibrated, instead, for governing a pre-revenue platform company through a technology qualification cycle that will be decided by engineering and supply-chain conversations, not by financing transactions. Whether the platform wins those conversations is the investment question. The board's composition suggests management understood what kind of governance the thesis required.
